outcome: The Experiment Library's browsing rules now have real behaviour tests
owner_impact: Nothing changes in what the Experiment Library shows or how it behaves. Its rules (which tabs you see as a guest, student or Professor, how collections, owners and researchers filter the list, how search works here or across all sources, the sort orders, the labels on each entry and every empty-state message) now live in one small module with 9 tests that check what happens, instead of tests that searched the code for exact lines. Test now: not needed — the Library's automatic checks at phone, foldable, desktop and ultra-wide sizes passed before and after publishing.

next.text: Next is #549 — a small ticket: every report will say clearly whether you should test and what, written into the workflow so GPT does it too, and the release wait tool will check every ~10 seconds instead of once a minute. #549 has not started.

technical_evidence: New web/src/library/browse.js (pure): source availability by role, per-source hierarchy filtering, context labels and search placeholders, search here/all, sort choices and ordering, row labels, revision badges, loaded-entry matching, results groups with empty and count texts.
experiment-library.js delegates those decisions (-211/+57 lines), texts unchanged; verify-dist checks the source labels in the built rules module.
New web/tests/library-browse.test.mjs: 9 behaviour tests; planted rule changes (Supervised for students, ignored 'All sources') are caught.
Retired only the 7 #480/#76 source-text assertions whose behaviour the new tests cover, replaced by checks that the Library uses the rules; 599 tests pass.
Style comparison of the built Lab identical to the current production build at all four viewports.
